central_question: What will the LME copper Official Settlement Price (cash, USD per tonne) be on 31 December 2027, given mine supply disruptions, new project ramps, the smelting TC/RC collapse, electrification demand, and US tariff policy?

situation_brief.current_situation: LME copper cash settled at 14,373.00 USD/t on 22 October 2026 [S1]; the IMF global price averaged a record 14,473.0559 USD/t in September 2026, +44.806% year-on-year [S3]. LME monthly-average stocks fell from a May 2026 peak of 394,892 t to 238,617 t in October 2026 [S12], with a US stockpile of roughly 1.6 Mt built ahead of a possible refined tariff [S19].
situation_brief.context: The 2026 spike reflects a genuine concentrate bottleneck — S&P Global estimates a 530,000 t 2026 concentrate deficit [S15]; the 2026 Antofagasta–Chinese smelter TC/RC benchmark settled at a record-low $0/t [S30] and Argus spot terms were −US$226.2/t on 18 September 2026 [S43]. ICSG (14 Oct 2026) forecasts a refined surplus of 104,000 t in 2026 widening to 368,000 t in 2027 as refined production grows 3.4% [S6]. Codelco H1 2026 output fell 11% year-on-year to 564,000 t [S5]; Cobre Panama remains shuttered with negotiations only recommended on 30 September 2026 [S37]. Section 232 tariffs: 50% on semi-finished copper since Aug 2025, refined cathode untariffed; Commerce recommended a 15% refined tariff from 1 Jan 2027 and 30% from 1 Jan 2028 [S8][S18]; COMEX–LME spread narrowed to ~$310–400/t [S19][S20].
situation_brief.dynamics: Concentrate shortage versus incoming refined supply: Kamoa-Kakula guides 500,000–540,000 t for 2027 [S38], Cochilco sees Chilean output +5.2% in 2027 [S28], while Chinese smelters (Tongling, Daye) begin output cuts into 2027 [S44]. Electrification, AI and data-centre demand drives ICSG usage growth of 2.5% in 2027, China at 59% of refined consumption [S6]. The near-flat COMEX curve holds ~$14,330–14,470/t into H1 2027 [S7]; sell-side forecasts ($11,000–12,125/t) sit lower [S25][S21][S26]. Historically ~24% annualized volatility; both completed ≥40% spikes retraced materially [S3].
fault_lines: Concentrate deficit (~530 kt) versus ICSG's projected 368 kt refined surplus in 2027
Deeply negative spot TC/RCs (−$226.2/t) versus smelter cutback discipline
US refined-tariff decision pulling metal into a ~1.6 Mt US stockpile while ex-US sits in a reported ~640 kt deficit
Cobre Panama restart: ~350 kt annual swing held hostage to Panamanian politics
Record prices versus 2–3-year historical retracement pattern
Chinese property drag versus electrification demand
catalysts: 1 Jan 2027 recommended start of 15% refined-copper tariff (SocGen risk-neutral 14.6% by Jan 2027; 37% for 30% by Jan 2028) [S18]
Q4 2026–Jan 2027 Antofagasta–Chinese smelter 2027 TC/RC benchmark talks [S30]
Panama–First Quantum negotiation outcome, potentially a signed restart agreement [S37]
Kamoa-Kakula 2027 ramp toward 500–540 kt [S38] and Cochilco's +5.2% Chilean rebound [S28]
31 Dec 2027 expiry of the Annex III floating-tariff framework [S52]
Anglo–Teck merger close expected by March 2027 [S39]

scenarios.name: Sustained supercycle
scenarios.narrative: Concentrate shortage, no Cobre Panama restart and record electrification demand keep the market in deficit, holding LME cash above $14,000/t at end-2027; prior: copper 20-25% annual vol makes sustained highs possible after a supply-driven spike.

scenarios.name: Elevated plateau
scenarios.narrative: New supply ramps and demand growth moderates, leaving prices in a $10,500-$14,000/t band at end-2027 with elevated but not extreme levels; prior: ±1 sigma bin around spot under 20-25% vol carries the most mass.

scenarios.name: Mean reversion
scenarios.narrative: Smelter cutbacks free concentrate, Cobre Panama partially restarts and high prices crush demand, returning prices to $7,500-$10,500/t; prior: copper spikes above trend have historically retraced within 2-3 years.

scenarios.name: Hard landing collapse
scenarios.narrative: A global recession or a tariff-war demand shock hits alongside supply recovery, driving prices below $7,500/t; prior: tail bin under copper volatility, requiring a named macro catalyst.

drivers.why_it_matters: A ~530,000 t concentrate deficit [S15] and negative spot terms (Argus −US$226.2/t on 18 Sep 2026) [S43] squeeze refined supply and support record prices.
Cuts of up to 30% of Tongling's primary capacity constrain refined output, eroding ICSG's projected 368,000 t 2027 surplus [S44].

drivers.variable: New mine supply ramp (Kamoa-Kakula, Chile rebound)
drivers.why_it_matters: Kamoa-Kakula guides 500,000–540,000 t for 2027 [S38] and Cochilco sees Chile +5.2% in 2027 [S28], supplying the surplus behind the elevated plateau.
A 368,000 t surplus on refined production +3.4% vs usage +2.5% caps prices if it materializes [S6].
A 15% refined tariff from 1 January 2027 would tighten ex-US supply, already shown by July 2026 US imports above 200,000 t, a 12-year high [S18].
ICSG attributes 2026-27 usage growth (+2.5% in 2027) to electrification, artificial intelligence and data centres [S6]; US retail electricity sales +4.602% y/y in Aug 2026 [S9].
A signed restart agreement (~350kt annual swing) would add supply expectations and bias mean reversion; only negotiations were recommended on 30 Sep 2026 [S37].
±1 sigma ≈ ±26% around spot spans the plateau band, concentrating mass in the $10,500–14,000/t range [S3].
